test_title: PYST 5: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following powers did Jammu and Kashmir have under Article 370?

options.text: Decision-making in all matters except defence, foreign affairs, and communications

solution:
The correct answer is __**All of the above**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 370** of the **Indian Constitution** provided a special autonomous status to the state of **Jammu and Kashmir**. This article allowed the state to have **its own Constitution**, which was separate from the Constitution of India. This document governed the internal administration and legal framework of the state. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• Under the provisions of **Article 370**, the state was permitted to fly its own **separate flag** alongside the **National Flag of India**. The state flag was **red** in color with **three white vertical stripes** representing the three regions of the state (Jammu, Kashmir, and Ladakh) and a **white plough**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

• The **Parliament of India** had limited legislative powers over the state. Its authority was restricted primarily to matters of **defence, foreign affairs, finance, and communications**. For the application of any other central laws, the **concurrence of the State Government** was mandatory, giving the state significant **decision-making power** in most internal matters. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• Because all the mentioned powers—having a separate constitution, a distinct flag, and restricted central legislative jurisdiction—were integral features of the special status granted by **Article 370**, the correct choice is **All of the above**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Historical Context:** **Article 370** was incorporated into the **Constitution of India** on **October 17, 1949**, as a **temporary provision**. It was drafted by **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar** to manage the unique transition of the state into the **Union of India** following the **Instrument of Accession** signed by **Maharaja Hari Singh** in **1947**.

• **Article 35A:** This was a significant provision derived from **Article 370**, introduced through a **Presidential Order in 1954**. It empowered the **Jammu and Kashmir State Legislature** to define **permanent residents** of the state and provide them with exclusive rights regarding **government jobs**, **scholarships**, and the **purchase of immovable property**.

• **Abrogation of Article 370:** On **August 5, 2019**, the **President of India** issued the **Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 2019**, which effectively revoked the special status. This action made the **Constitution of India** fully applicable to the region and ended the state's separate constitution and flag.

• **Reorganization:** Following the abrogation, the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019** was enacted. This led to the **bifurcation** of the state into two **Union Territories**: **Jammu and Kashmir** (with a legislative assembly) and **Ladakh** (without a legislative assembly), effective from **October 31, 2019**.

**Important Points__**

• **Legislative Impact:** Before **2019**, **Article 360** (Financial Emergency) of the Indian Constitution did not apply to **Jammu and Kashmir**. Furthermore, the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and various **Fundamental Rights** were applicable only in a modified form or through state-specific legislation.

• **Judicial Oversight:** While the **Supreme Court of India** had jurisdiction over the state, the **High Court of Jammu and Kashmir** held a unique position, and certain central laws like the **Right to Information (RTI) Act** or the **Right to Education (RTE) Act** were not automatically applicable until the state legislature passed corresponding laws.

• **Current Status:** Since **October 2019**, the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** has replaced the **Ranbir Penal Code (RPC)**, and all **central laws** and **welfare schemes** are now directly implemented in the **Union Territories** of **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
